newsitem.title: NORWAY: Ekofisk output may be resumed on Monday - Phillips.
newsitem.headline: Ekofisk output may be resumed on Monday - Phillips.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum said on Monday it hoped to restart oil production at the North Sea Ekofisk field later in the day.
The 350,000 barrel per day Ekofisk development was shut in last Tuesday after a gas leak was detected in a 30-inch oil pipeline.
"We are hoping to be able to start up after lunch today," Phillips spokesman Sander Bull-Gjertsen said, adding that work to replace a section of the pipeline was still going on.
"We are adjusting new pipes to old systems and that is causing extra problems," he said.
"When we start up again normal production will be exceeded for about four days because of pressure built up during the shutdown," he said.
Output from third party fields -- British Petroleum's Gyda and Ula and Amoco's Valhall and Hod -- and the Statpipe gas line was uninterupted by the shutdown.
